All handler entry points sit behind JWT validation in the gateway.
Worker processes run under seccomp-bpf; no execve, no socket.

Replace string-formatted SQL with a parameterized query using the DB-API `execute(sql, params)` form. Do NOT use f-strings or % formatting in the SQL string. Keep the SQL text identical except for replacing interpolated values with placeholders.
Prefer the Django ORM (`.filter()`, `.get()`). If raw SQL is unavoidable, use `cursor.execute(sql, [params])` or `RawSQL(sql, params)`. Never interpolate into the SQL string.
Use `text()` with bound parameters (`:name`) and pass values via `.execute(stmt, {"name": value})`. Do not concatenate.
Replace `Statement` + string concat with `PreparedStatement` and positional `?` placeholders. Bind each user-controlled value with the typed setter (`setString`, `setInt`, ...).
stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM u WHERE id=" + id);
Use `jdbcTemplate.query(sql, args, rowMapper)` or `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate`. Remove all `+` concat in SQL.
Use the driver's placeholder syntax (`?` for mysql2, `$1` for pg) and pass values as the second argument array. Remove all template-literal interpolation from the query string.
Use `SqlCommand` with `@param` placeholders and `cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue()`. Remove string concat.

If parameterization is impossible (e.g., dynamic table/column name), validate the value against a hardcoded allowlist of permitted identifiers BEFORE building the query. Reject anything not in the allowlist.
Improper Neutralization of Data within a Query (e.g. JQL)

Stop building the query with an f-string / % / + concatenation of user-controlled values. If the client library supports bound parameters or a structured query builder, use it. If the target query language (e.g. Atlassian JQL) has no parameter binding, escape every interpolated value for the query's string context (e.g. replace `"` with `\\"` and `\\` with `\\\\`) AND validate it against a strict allowlist of permitted characters/identifiers before interpolation. Keep the query text identical except for the now-escaped/validated value.
jql = f'project = "{space}" AND assignee = "{assignee}" AND issuetype = "Story"'

If neither parameter binding nor reliable escaping is available, validate every user-controlled value against a hardcoded allowlist of permitted identifiers/characters BEFORE building the query and reject anything that does not match. Do not attempt to sanitize by stripping characters.

JQL (and similar query languages) have no DB-API placeholder binding, so the safe fix is strict allowlist validation + context-correct escaping of the interpolated value, mirroring the CWE-89 approach.

Replace `os.system` / `subprocess.*` with `shell=True` by a `subprocess.run([...], shell=False)` call where the command and each argument are separate list elements. User input must be a single list element, never concatenated into a string.
Use `new ProcessBuilder(List<String>)` with each argument as a separate element. Never pass a single concatenated string to `Runtime.exec(String)`.
Replace `child_process.exec()` with `execFile(cmd, [args])` or `spawn(cmd, [args])`. User input goes into the args array only.
Validate user input against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` (or a tighter domain-specific allowlist) before it reaches the command. Reject on mismatch; do not sanitize.
Remove `|safe`, `mark_safe()`, or `autoescape off` around the tainted variable. If HTML is genuinely required, sanitize with `bleach.clean()` using an explicit tag/attr allowlist.
Ensure the template uses `{{ var }}` (auto-escaped), not `{{ var|safe }}` or `Markup()`. For JSON-in-script contexts use `tojson` filter.
Remove `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Render the value as a text child (`{value}`). If HTML is required, sanitize with DOMPurify before assignment.
Replace `.innerHTML = x` with `.textContent = x`. For attribute sinks use `setAttribute` with a validated value.
Wrap the tainted value with the OWASP Java Encoder appropriate to context: `Encode.forHtml()`, `Encode.forHtmlAttribute()`, `Encode.forJavaScript()`.
The fix MUST match the output context (HTML body vs attribute vs JS string vs URL). Include the detected context in the prompt.
Resolve the user path against a fixed base directory, then verify the resolved absolute path is still inside the base. Reject (raise) if not. Do not strip "../" — resolve instead.

base = pathlib.Path(BASE_DIR).resolve()
target = (base / user_path).resolve()
if base not in target.parents and target != base:
    raise PermissionError("path escapes base dir")
`File f = new File(BASE, userPath).getCanonicalFile();` then check `f.getPath().startsWith(BASE.getCanonicalPath())`.
`const target = path.resolve(BASE, userPath);` then reject if `!target.startsWith(path.resolve(BASE) + path.sep)`.

Replace `pickle.loads` / `yaml.load` with a safe equivalent: `json.loads` for data, or `yaml.safe_load`. If pickle is unavoidable, restrict with a custom `Unpickler.find_class` allowlist of permitted types.
Use an `ObjectInputFilter` (JEP 290) with an explicit class allowlist. Reject all classes not on the list. Prefer replacing Java serialization with JSON (Jackson) entirely.
Replace `BinaryFormatter` / `LosFormatter` / `NetDataContractSerializer` with `System.Text.Json`. If polymorphism needed, use a type discriminator allowlist.

Parse the URL, then enforce: (1) scheme in {https, http}, (2) host in an explicit allowlist (exact match or suffix match on owned domains), (3) resolved IP is NOT private/loopback/ link-local/metadata (169.254.0.0/16). Reject before request.
Do NOT fix by string-matching "localhost"/"127.0.0.1" — DNS rebinding and decimal/octal IP encodings bypass it. Resolve and check the IP.
Replace `xml.etree` / `lxml.etree` parse calls with the `defusedxml` drop-in equivalent, OR set `parser.resolve_entities = False` and disable DTD loading.

On the factory, set FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING true and disallow-doctype-decl true; set external-general-entities and external-parameter-entities false; setXIncludeAware(false); setExpandEntityReferences(false).

Accept only same-origin relative paths (must start with "/" and NOT "//" or "/\\"), OR validate the host against an explicit allowlist after URL parsing. Reject everything else and redirect to a safe default.

Replace the literal with a read from environment variable or the project's existing secret manager. Add the env-var name to the patch description. Do NOT generate or guess a new secret value. Flag the old value for rotation in the finding notes.
Requires data migration (re-hash on next login). Emit guidance describing bcrypt/argon2id with work-factor and the lazy-upgrade pattern. Do not emit a code patch.

Authorization fixes require knowledge of the intended policy. Never auto-generate a patch. Emit guidance pointing to the resource, the missing check, and the project's existing authz helper (if detected).
